issues.note: Explanation and learner-error note agree; although does take short adjective phrases.
The qualifying 'but' use differs in position and often translation; the split is justified.
If is not a word learners confuse with although; unexplained compare item.
Ungrammatical although...but example contradicts the explanation and learner error.
Definition fits the qualifying use and all its examples.
When is a time word, not a confusable of although.
Although plus adjective phrase (although expensive) is standard; fine description for learners.
False origin; although comes from Middle English all + though.
Elliptical use is covered in sense 2 explanation and example.
Concessive while is a genuine near-synonym of although.
Register reversed: although is more formal, though more common in speech.
Sentence-final although is nonstandard; the note is correct for learners.
But is a close synonym in the qualifying use (good, but expensive).
Example models the although...but error the entry warns against.

findings.F1: Sense 1 example 'Although she was tired, but she stayed up to help' is ungrammatical and contradicts the entry.
findings.F2: Synonym discrimination reverses register: although is the more formal one, and though is more common in speech.
findings.F3: Etymology is false: although is all + though, not Latin alter through French.
findings.F4: if-conj in sense 1 compare is not a confusable word.
findings.F5: when-conj in sense 1 compare is not a confusable word.
